A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
leaf photosynthetic performance scales with water transport capacity in tropical canopy trees, and that this relationship may be mediated by wood density.
water transport capacity and photosynthesis are co-ordinated at the branch level, and that this coordination varies among species in relation to wood density and water storage capacity.
the leaf photosynthetic capacity of a tree is proportional to the water transport capacity of its branches, which in turn is constrained by the density of wood in the branches.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the water transport capacity of a tree branch is related to the photosynthetic capacity of the leaves on that branch.

leaf level measurements of photosynthesis and gas exchange should be coupled with measurements of branch hydraulic conductivity and wood properties in order to understand the mechanisms of species differences in photosynthetic performance and water use efficiency.
water transport capacity is an important determinant of leaf photosynthetic performance.
